A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRAPHTREX research. The complete main texts, references, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison despite appendix reordering and visual revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original I2B2 and English E3C experiments, including model comparisons, ablations, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds attention-baseline results and relation-class performance analysis.

M1.justification: The span encoder, graph construction, HGT refinement, losses, and prediction procedure are retained. Expanded masking instructions and the iterative architecture diagram explain procedures already documented in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate I2B2 and the English E3C subset with the same task coverage. E3C already appears in v1's experiments; its addition to the abstract is not new coverage. The classwise analysis examines existing relation labels.

E2.justification: V2 adds the multi-head attention comparator attributed to Miller et al. (2023) to both I2B2 and E3C comparisons in Tables 1–2. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The new classwise evaluation filters I2B2 predictions and gold graphs by relation type and flips gold Before/After links before scoring (Section 5.4). V2 also specifies a shared entity-extraction setup for the added attention baseline. Existing splits, training budgets, and aggregate evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds relation-class performance analysis in Table 6 and reports that increasing or decreasing the attention baseline's head count reduces performance. Existing distance, graph-component, encoder, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 5.3 newly identifies the paired t-test underlying the unchanged p-value of 4.26 × 10^-9. This clarifies existing significance reporting without documenting additional runs, seeds, or uncertainty intervals.

E6.justification: New results include attention-baseline TLink F1 scores of 44.24 on I2B2 and 3.97 on E3C, plus class-specific scores in Table 6. Existing aggregate and appendix results are retained, including GRAPHTREX's respective TLink F1 scores of 68.81 and 23.48.

T1.justification: The mathematical graph definitions, representation and HGT equations, losses, and temporal-awareness metric definitions are retained. Neither version adds formal propositions, theorems, or proofs relative to the other.

C1.justification: The principal claims about I2B2 performance, long-range relations, E3C generalization, and BioMedBERT-UMLS are retained. The E3C claim newly included in the abstract was already present in v1's introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: V2 proposes a context-based explanation for the attention baseline's weaker relation extraction and relates classwise performance to label imbalance. Existing applicability boundaries, dataset-access limitations, and human-oversight qualifications are substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 replaces a promised future code release with a stated public repository link. Appendix S3 expands masking instructions, and S5 specifies 128 attention heads of 64 dimensions for the new baseline. Existing hardware and training details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Miller et al. (2023) as a relevant attention-based comparison and Yao et al. (2024) for chemotherapy timeline extraction, while removing the Ul Haq et al. exclusion citation. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 makes local prose revisions, expands the sliding-window explanation into numbered steps, and reorders appendices, notably moving data and implementation details earlier. The main section sequence and most of the narrative are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 receive substantial visual revisions: a horizontal example layout, clearer pre/post-HGT edge distinctions, and numbered architecture stages with an iteration loop. V2 also adds Table 6, expands baseline tables, enlarges Figure S1, and rearranges appendix displays.

improvement.justification: The additional contemporary comparator and classwise diagnostics modestly strengthen the evaluation. Clearer method diagrams, fuller masking instructions, identification of the statistical test, and concrete code-access information improve transparency. These are useful, bounded gains; the core method and existing empirical findings remain unchanged.
